headlines.title: No evidence injured girl was involved in Redwood City crash, police say
headlines.description: Authorities have found no evidence to back up a report that an injured girl was spotted at the scene of a rollover crash Sunday night in Redwood City, police said. The crash occurred about 10:40 p.m. on northbound U.S. Highway 101 at the overpass north of Woodside Road. The suspect fled the scene on foot, authorities said. Police and California Highway Patrol officers searched the area following a report that a 4- to 5-year-old girl, with blonde or brown hair and a pink jacket, was seen bleeding from the head after the crash. “After a thorough search, no juvenile matching the reported description was located and there is currently no evidence that a child was involved,” police said in an update on Monday morning.

headlines.title: Bay Area home prices keep rising despite typical fall slowdown
headlines.description: Home prices continue to rise across the Bay Area, even as the housing market typically begins to cool in the fall. The latest Zillow Home Value Index shows home values rose across all nine Bay Area counties in August. San Francisco saw a 1.8% increase, while San Mateo County rose 0.7% and Alameda County increased 0.1%. Home values in the remaining counties rose by roughly a couple tenths of a percentage point. Coldwell Banker told NBC Bay Area it is not seeing the typical slowdown in fall sales activity that the region has experienced in recent years. The real estate company said there is a significant amount of cash in the market, in part because of the boom in artificial intelligence. “Even though interest rates have ticked up, those buyers that are mortgage dependent are still coming into the market and they want home ownership,” said Mary Lee Blaylock, president of Coldwell Banker Affiliates. “The American Dream of home ownership is steadfast and consistent and remains intact no matter what.” Coldwell Banker said it cannot predict where home prices will go from here and noted that real estate conditions can vary significantly from one area to another. The company recommends consulting with a local real estate agent when considering buying or selling a home.

headlines.title: Bay Area voter guide: What to know about the November 2026 election
headlines.description: What to Know — Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026 California will choose a new governor to replace Gavin Newsom, who terms out after this year. The choices are Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton. Voters will decide 14 state propositions. Regional sales tax Measure RTM, the Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, aims to increase funds for public transit. California’s Congressional District 11 race features Scott Wiener and Connie Chan competing to succeed Nancy Pelosi. Aisha Wahab and Melissa Hernandez will face off again after a special election in August where Wahab secured victory to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. All 80 California Assembly seats are up for reelection, as well as 20 Senate seats. California’s general election is Nov. 3, with statewide races and propositions as well as key local races and measures across the Bay Area. Here’s what you need to know to cast your ballot, including important dates and deadlines, how to register or check your status, where and when to vote, and what’s on the ballot. Key election dates The last day to register to vote for the Nov. 3 general election is Oct. 19. County election officials will start mailing ballots by Oct. 5. Ballot drop-off locations open on Oct. 6 Last day to register to vote for the general election is Oct. 19. First vote centers open for early in-person voting in all Voter’s Choice Act counties on Oct. 24. In person early voting locations in the state open on Oct. 31. Election Day, Nov. 3, is the last day to vote in-person or return a ballot by 8 p.m. Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Vote-by-mail ballots must be postmarked no later than Nov. 3. If mailing on election day, get a hand-stamped postmark from a postal employee inside a post office. Visit the California Secretary of State’s website for a full list of key dates and deadlines. Check voter registration status Voters can check their registration at voterstatus.sos.ca.gov to confirm their mailing address and voting status. How to register to vote California residents can register to vote in elections at registertovote.ca.gov. Note Oct. 19 is the last day to register for the general election. Same day voter registration window will be open from Oct. 20 up to the Nov. 3 election day. Visit caearlyvoting.sos.ca.gov for a list of early voting locations to complete same day registration. How to find your polling place Visit the California Secretary of State’s website, where you can input your address to find your polling location and see what is on your ballot. Voters can also visit their county elections office for more information. Scroll down to the Bay Area county election offices section of this guide for further contact information. What to bring to your polling place Voters usually are not required to show identification to a polling place worker before casting a ballot, according to the Secretary of State’s website. There are some instances when providing identification is required: Voting for the first time after registering to vote by mail and did not provide a driver license number California identification number or the last four digits of social security number are missing on registration form In these cases voters should plan to bring identification to a polling place or bring a copy of it with their vote-by-mail ballot. The Secretary of State says the following are acceptable forms of identification: Passport Driver license Official state identification card Student identification card Copy of recent utility bill Sample ballot booklet received from county elections office Any document received by a government agency How to track your mail-in ballot Voters can track their vote-by-mail ballot and confirm it has been received by using the state’s Where’s My Ballot? tool at california.ballottrax.net/voter/. Ballots mailed in may take a few days to appear on the website. Why is California choosing a new governor? Gov. Gavin Newsom terms out after this year and voters will choose between Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton, who both advanced to the general election after a wild primary. Becerra has served as former President Joe Biden’s top health official and oversaw the response to the coronavirus pandemic. He was also the California’s attorney general during President Donald Trump’s first term and has more than two decades of experience as a congressmember. Hilton was a conservative commentator with a show on Fox News for six years. He also worked as an adviser to former British prime minister David Cameron. What are the 14 California propositions voters will decide in the November election? Here’s a list of the California propositions on the November ballot and descriptions from the secretary of state: Proposition 1: Authorizes bonds for housing affordability programs Proposition 2: Increases state’s rainy day fund Proposition 3: Provides permanent funding for schools and healthcare by extending existing tax on high incomes Proposition 4: Repeals prohibition against public funding of election campaigns. Proposition 5: Changes recall election process for statewide officers. Proposition 37: Creates loan program for middle-income buyers of qualified new homes. Proposition 38: Authorizes bonds for immunology medical research. Proposition 39: Prohibits citizens from voting unless they present government-issued identification. Proposition 40: Imposes one-time tax on certain taxpayers. Proposition 41: Prohibits new state taxes that exclude revenues from state spending limit. Requires audits for new state special taxes. Proposition 42: Prohibits new state personal property taxes and certain retroactive state taxes. Proposition 43: Limits voters’ ability to raise revenues for local government services. Proposition 44: Requires community health clinics spend 90% of revenue on program services. Proposition 45: Modifies environmental review for certain projects. Regional measure to watch Measure RTM: The Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, is a regional sales tax aimed at increasing funds for public transit. It includes 5 Bay Area counties: Alameda, Contra Costa, San Francisco, San Mateo, and Santa Clara. Races and measures to watch in Alameda County California Congressional District 14: California lawmaker Aisha Wahab and Bay Area Rapid Transit Director Melissa Hernandez will face off again to determine who will serve the next full two-year term. Wahab topped Hernandez in an August special election to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. Swalwell resigned from Congress earlier this year after sexual assault and misconduct allegations. District 14 includes the East Bay cities such as Fremont, Hayward and Livermore. Measure X in Berkeley: Would establish 10% limit on annual rent increases and other changes to the city’s rent ordinance. Measure Y in Berkeley: Parcel tax to pay for arts projects. Measure Z in Berkeley: Parcel tax to fund a public bank. Measure AA in Berkeley: Increase soda tax (not assigned) Measure EE in Oakland: Shift city to a strong mayor system. Measure FF in Oakland: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Alameda County and additional election information, visit the Alameda County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Contra Costa County In Contra Costa County, several county board of education seats are open. In Richmond, residents will vote on a new mayor while voters in San Pablo will weigh in on Measure S, which would limit rent increases. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Contra Costa County and additional election information, visit the Contra Costa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Napa County California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. Measure B in Napa County: Sales tax to fund wildfire prevention and open space preservation. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Napa County and additional election information, visit the Napa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Francisco San Francisco voters will weigh in on several open seats on the county board of supervisors and board of education. Proposition A: Give mayor more power to hire and fire department heads. Proposition B: Pave way for public bank. Proposition C: Increase the city’s annual contribution to an affordable housing trust fund. Proposition D: New barriers to placing measures on the ballot. Proposition E: Changes to city contracting. Proposition G: Reopen parts of the Great Highway to vehicle traffic on weekdays. Proposition H: Parcel tax to fund Muni. Proposition J: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax California Congressional District 11: Scott Wiener and Connie Chan compete to succeed Nancy Pelosi. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Francisco and additional election information, visit the San Francisco Department of Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Mateo County Measure E in Redwood City: Limit rent increases. Measure Q in Half Moon Bay: Referendum to block proposed farmworker housing. Measure U in San Mateo County: Create independent commission to draw supervisor districts. For a complete list of San Mateo County measures and races on the ballot, visit smacre.gov/elections. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Mateo County and additional election information, visit the San Mateo County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Santa Clara County In San Jose, incumbents Peter Ortiz and Bien Doan are up for re-election in Districts 5 and 7, respectively, and there’s an open seat in District 9. Races and measures to watch in Solano County Solano County Board of Supervisors, District 4: Mike Silva and John Carli face in a runoff in a district covering Vacaville and Dixon. Measure E in Solano County: New tax on data centers and battery storage facilities in the unincorporated county areas. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Solano County and additional election information, visit the Solano County Registrar of Voters website. Races and measures to watch in Sonoma County California Congressional District 1: Mike McGuire will face James Gallagher in a seat redistricted by Proposition 50. California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. State Assembly District 12: Eric Lucan and Jackie Elward compete in a battle between business and labor. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Sonoma County and additional election information, visit the Sonoma County Registrar of Voters website. headlines.title: Weekend shooting leaves 1 dead in Oakland's Grand Lake neighborhood
headlines.description: Police are investigating after a man was fatally shot early Sunday in Oakland’s Grand Lake neighborhood. The shooting occurred shortly before 2 a.m. in the 3200 block of Grand Avenue, near the Grand Lake Theater, Oakland police said. After the shooting was reported, officers responded and attempted life-saving measures, and the victim was transported to a hospital where he died. Police didn’t release any information on circumstances surrounding the shooting or a suspect description. Anyone with information, video, or photos related to the shooting is asked to contact the Oakland police homicide section at 510-238-3821. The tip line is 510-238-7950.

headlines.title: Protesters rally at Bonta's Oakland office to stop Paramount-Warner Bros. merger
headlines.description: A protest outside California Attorney General Rob Bonta’s Oakland office caught the attention of some of the biggest names in Hollywood on Sunday. About three dozen demonstrators protested at Bonta’s office with a mission to persuade him to continue his fight against the Paramount-Warner Brothers merger and not accept what they say is a bad settlement. More than 1,000 actors, directors and production crews, including 75 Academy Award winners, have come out against the merger. The group formed after actor Mark Ruffalo encouraged his social media followers to join the rally. Paramount Skydance wants to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery for about $110 billion. But the deal has been met with political and legal challenges, as well as with protests. Among other things, opponents are worried it will hurt writers and shrink the labor market. “It’s the tens of thousands of people who will lose their jobs, the creativity that will be lost as a result of there not being this competition out there,” Landmark Theaters co-founder Gary Mayer said. Paramount has said publicly it needs the merger so it can compete financially with larger companies, but in July, California joined 11 other states in suing to stop the merger, and a judge temporarily blocked the consolidation deal during litigation. In an email, Bonta’s press office said they could not “confirm or deny” whether talks are ongoing nor about “their alleged substance.” Protestors say they want Bonta and other AGs across the country to stand firmly against further media consolidation, stop the settlement talks and take this case to trial. NBC Bay Area reached out to Paramount for comment about the rally and the ongoing talks but have not heard back.

headlines.title: Spot fires burn more than 300 acres in Marin County
headlines.description: Multiple spot fires ended up burning approximately 340 acres in Marin County on Sunday, the Marin County Fire said. The fire department said at around 4:40 p.m. crews responded to reports of a vegetation fire near Chileno Valley Road, around four miles south of Tomales Road, in the Chileno Valley area. Upon arrival, the fire department said it was determined there were multiple spot fires. The forward progress of one of the smaller ones was stopped at around 4:50 p.m., while the forward progress of the two remaining fires was stopped just before 7 p.m. Authorities said the spot fires burned approximately 340 acres combined.

headlines.title: Giants legend Duane Kuiper reveals throat cancer diagnosis, undergoing treatment
headlines.description: SAN FRANCISCO — Kruk and Kuip plan to call their final game together on Sept. 27, but the road to get there won’t be easy. A few weeks after Mike Krukow announced that this will be his final season, Duane Kuiper revealed Sunday that he has been diagnosed with throat cancer. Kuiper is getting treatment and will miss some upcoming games, but he plans to be in the booth next weekend with Krukow for their final series together. “I was recently diagnosed with throat cancer and began treatment last week with my doctors at Stanford Medicine,” Kuiper said in a statement released by the Giants. “This cancer is unrelated to the one I experienced five years ago, and I’m optimistic that it will be successfully treated. I’ll miss the broadcasts tomorrow and Wednesday as I continue treatment, but I’m looking forward to returning Tuesday and this weekend to celebrate my partner, Mike Krukow, and his remarkable career as he calls his final game before retirement. I’m incredibly grateful for the care I’m receiving and for the tremendous support from my family, the Giants organization, my broadcast partners and so many others.” Kuiper, 76, missed this weekend’s series against the Los Angeles Dodgers, with Jon Miller and Dave Flemming filling in. He has long planned to be back next weekend, when he and Krukow, his broadcast partner and closest friend, will call games against the Dodgers for the final time. It will be the end of a 36-year run for Krukow, who announced last month that he is retiring because his long battle with inclusion body myositis has made it difficult to continue to keep up with the physical demands of the job. Kuiper, who underwent chemotherapy in 2021, has said that he intends to keep calling games beyond this season. headlines.title: Body found in Guadalupe River Trail area in San Jose
headlines.description: A body was found in the Guadalupe River Trail area in San Jose early Sunday morning, according to the police department. Police said at around 1:15 a.m., officers responded to a report of suspicious circumstance in the area of the Guadalupe River Trail near the intersection of Coleman Avenue and Autumn Parkway. There, authorities said they found a dead person. The police department said investigation is ongoing.

headlines.title: 2 killed in firefighting helicopter crash at Dome Fire in Yosemite
headlines.description: Two people fighting the Dome Fire in Yosemite died after their firefighting helicopter crashed Sunday, according to officials. The helicopter crashed around 2 p.m. The cause of the crash was not immediately known. Aerospace company FlyPrecision announced on social media that it had lost two members of its team, saying the company was “devastated by this loss.” The Dome Fire has burned more than 3,000 acres and was 15% contained. No evacuation orders were in place.

headlines.title: California establishes Sept. 25 as Dolly Parton Day under new law
headlines.description: California has officially established Sept. 25 as Dolly Parton Day in honor of the renowned singer, songwriter, philanthropist and actress, the governor’s office announced Sunday. Gov. Gavin Newsom signed Senate Bill 931, authored by State Senators Shannon Grove, R-Bakersfield, and John Laird, D-Santa Cruz. The date — 9/25 — was selected as a clever nod to Parton’s beloved hit song “9 to 5,” according to the governor’s office. “We could all afford to live a little more like Dolly. Be kind, be humble, and have some fun… Be a diamond in a rhinestone world,” Newsom said in a statement. “With this bill, we are not just establishing a day to celebrate Dolly Parton, we are creating an annual reminder to us, every year, to live the way she did — joyfully, graciously, and with a whole lot of heart.” Dubbed the “Queen of Country,” Parton is celebrated as one of the most successful country music performers in history, having sold more than 100 million records worldwide. Over her six-decade career, she achieved 25 number-one hits — the most by any female country artist. Her iconic anthem “I Will Always Love You” topped the charts twice, in 1974 and 1982, before Whitney Houston later covered it to enormous global acclaim. Beyond music, Parton built an enduring legacy in acting, producing, and business. Her contributions to Hollywood include her acting debut in the feminist comedy film “9 to 5,” as well as both the 1992 film and the hit television series “Buffy the Vampire Slayer,” for which she served as an uncredited producer. Lawmakers emphasized that Parton’s impact stretches far beyond entertainment, particularly highlighting her humanitarian work and commitment to early childhood literacy through the Imagination Library. The program has distributed more than 300 million books to children worldwide, including across California. “Dolly Parton sparkled on every stage she ever stood on, but her brightest sparkle was the literacy legacy she built through the Imagination Library,” Grove said. “I am incredibly proud of the bipartisan work we have accomplished, from bringing her bilingual reading program statewide in California with former Senate President pro Tempore Toni Atkins, to introducing a bipartisan bill with Senator Laird to establish this annual day of remembrance.” The love Dolly gave so freely, rooted in her deep and openly shared faith, and the love the world returned to her, shows how deeply she was cherished by everyone. I thank Governor Newsom for signing SB 931 so that every September 25th, our state will remember the legend who put millions of books in the hands of our youngest readers and inspired the world on how to respect and love one another,” Grove added. Laird echoed those sentiments, noting Parton’s deep ties to the state. “I’m grateful to Governor Newsom for signing our bill and to Senator Grove for her partnership in making September 25 Dolly Parton Day in California,” Laird said in a statement. “Dolly brought joy to a lot of people, but her legacy goes well beyond her music. Through the Imagination Library, she put books into the hands of millions of children, and throughout her life she led with kindness, acceptance, and a belief that everyone deserves to be treated with dignity and respect. She was also no stranger to the Central Coast, where she performed for packed crowds and spent time over the years. Now, every 9-2-5, California gets to celebrate Dolly and the remarkable legacy she shared with all of us,” Laird said. headlines.title: Oakland Roots reach agreement to develop Howard Terminal site
headlines.description: The Oakland Roots Soccer Club, Port of Oakland and a Southern California realty group have come to an exploratory negotiating agreement to develop the Howard Terminal site. On Sept. 10, the Port of Oakland Commissioners voted to authorize an exploratory exclusive negotiating agreement with the team, the port and Industrial Realty Group for one year at Howard Terminal, according to an agenda report. “You are probably aware that we have been playing at four different venues through our seven years existence, very nomadic,” Chief Real Estate Officer of the Oakland Roots and Soul Lydia Tan said. “I think it’s important for me personally as a commissioner to think about the opportunities at Howard as something that will provide strength and health to the entire port and all of our operations, and I think this is really good step in that direction.” A description of the respective projects, site plans, proposed acreage parking plans, potential uses, workforce and maritime integration are part of the expected timeline. in a statement, the Oakland 68s, an organization dedicated to the community and its sports culture said in part the agreement “represents an opportunity to build a new chapter for Oakland sports and the city’s waterfront.” NBC Bay Area reached out to Industrial Realty Group for comment, but hasn’t heard back yet.

headlines.title: Baby born in San Francisco traffic after family pulls over for 911 help
headlines.description: A healthy baby girl made an unexpected roadside arrival Friday afternoon after her family got stuck in heavy traffic on the way to the hospital, according to the San Francisco Fire Department. The unexpected delivery began at approximately 4:40 p.m., when crews received a report of a family en route to a hospital to deliver their baby, the department announced Saturday. Fire officials said due to heavy traffic near Crossover Drive and Martin Luther King Jr. Drive, the family pulled over and called 911. SFFD Paramedic Engine 14 and AMR Unit 110, a 911 provider for San Francisco, were dispatched to the scene. AMR Unit 110 arrived first, but traffic conditions forced the crew to park two blocks away and run to reach the patient. Parents Karollyn and Nate said on Sunday a doula sitting in traffic with them helped coach Karollyn through the process while waiting for paramedics. Personnel arrived just in time to assist with the delivery of the baby girl. Engine 14 crews arrived shortly afterward to provide care for both the mother and the newborn. Both the mother and child were later transported to a local hospital and reported to be in good condition, the department stated. “We want to congratulate the family and welcome this new child to the world,” the SFFD said in a statement. “Her arrival is a true testament to the dedication, compassion and teamwork of our first responders.” On Sunday, Karollyn and Nate revealed the baby’s name is Cielle Ray. They said Karollyn is “doing great,” and she is in the recovery process. “Mom is doing great, recovering well and we’re leaving later tonight,” the family wrote. “We always joked around about giving birth in the car, never thought it would happen to us. We took a route that I take every morning to work without issues, and just so happens that the day with the worst traffic is the last day we needed it. But we were so fortunate to have the support that we did, especially some medical professionals that were sitting in the same traffic. Most notably a doula that helped coach Karollyn through the process until the paramedics arrived.
